$why: THE LIST IS THIS REPO'S OWN FACT, not a fleet default: the engine refuses (exit 2)
rather than guess, so an undeclared toolchain is silently unguarded.
cargo/rustc: the workspace's primary long jobs (build, test, clippy, nextest) —
minutes, dependency-heavy, the workload offload exists for.
npm/npx/vitest: the csq/ui Svelte suite (vitest + svelte-check).
DELIBERATELY NOT DECLARED, each for the same reason — the guard's cost is
attention, and a guard that reds on trivial invocations gets uninstalled
(runbook § 'The false-positive corpus is the whole risk'):
python3 / node — routinely invoked here as one-line gates and --check syntax
probes (score()s of these run per session, nearly all sub-second). Declaring
them would put an advisory on almost every tool call.
If a specific long python3/node job recurs, wrap THAT call in `trestle run --`
by hand rather than declaring the interpreter repo-wide.
KNOWN BOUNDARY, documented rather than hidden: read_only_flags applies to the flag
in the program's OWN argument slot, so `cargo --version` is clean but
`cargo build --help` is a finding. That is the engine's semantics, not a csq
widening candidate; do not silence the hook over it (rules/offload-discipline.md
MUST NOT 2).
local_only: programs that must run on THIS Mac and are never moved to a remote:
dev-install.sh installs the CLI into ~/.local/bin and Developer-ID-signs it;
release-enterprise-macos.sh signs and notarizes with this Mac's keychain identity.
Matched by basename. Everything else is portable and goes unpinned
(rules/offload-discipline.md MUST-1).
